author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if everything you've ever been motivated to do, and everything you've avoided doing, could be explained by the same 12 forces?

Bestselling author of Intentional and Hyperfocus, Chris Bailey, walks you through an interactive thought experiment that reveals your hidden values: the 12 fundamental forces driving every decision you make. Based on the latest research across hundreds of thousands of participants in 80+ countries, this isn't a simple personality quiz: it’s the real science of what motivates you.

By trying the "would you rather" exercise along with the audience, you can begin to discover your own values. Chris also shares the story of why he (a productivity expert) quit a marathon, embraced his own laziness, and finally stopped feeling guilty about it. Chris Bailey has been described by TED as ‘the most productive man you’d ever hope to meet’. His 2019 TEDxManchester Talk (How to Get Your Brain to Focus) with nearly 20m views is one of the all-time most popular TEDx Tal
title: 12 things that motivate everything you do | Chris Bailey | TEDxManchester

description: Amidst the current geopolitical and environmental strains, Dr. Raúl Hinojosa-Ojeda parse through the top three prompts in humanity’s final exam – Global Rebalancing, Nature crisis, and AI. Packing into the talk is a 2000 year galloping timeline of changing global North-South dynamics, a spotlight on the global Indigenous, Migrant, Frontline communities, and an AI companion tool to unpack the talk further: https://tedtalkagent.netlify.app/.  UCLA professor and University of Chicago–trained political economist Dr. Raúl Hinojosa-Ojeda has spent decades decoding the intricate currents of trade, migration, and regional integration across the Americas and the Pacific Rim. A scholar with an emphasis on real-world impact, he is a founding director of UCLA’s North American Integration and Development (NAID) Center in 1995 and co-conceiving the $3 billion North American Development Bank in 1994. His strategic counsel has shaped key transnational institutions as well as federal economic oversigh
title: Great Global Rebalancing, Nature Crisis and Cross Border AI Agents | Raúl Hinojosa-Ojeda | TEDxUCLA

author: TEDx Talks
description: What are your shoulds costing you? One honest question—“Is this mine?”—can help you let go of inherited expectations and live your life by design. Lizz Welch is a Certified High Performance Coach, Dream Builder, and Founder of Unleash Impact, dedicated to empowering purpose-driven leaders and organizations. As a former global CEO and COO of a iDE, a nonprofit that doubled its impact under her leadership, and with over two decades of experience delivering social impact, Lizz combines strategic clarity with compassionate leadership. She is passionate about women’s economic empowerment and helping mission-driven leaders and businesses to scale while increasing joy in their lives. Lizz is a Returned Morocco Peace Corps volunteer and has lived and worked across more than 30 countries. She writes and speaks on gender, economic development, leadership, non-profits, philanthropy, high performance, and finance. When she’s not coaching or consulting, she enjoys cooking, walking, photography, mu
title: The High Cost of Shoulds | Elizabeth Welch | TEDxManitou Springs Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description: Electricity is the invisible force behind almost everything that makes modern civilisation possible—but what happens when our growing dependence on it begins to threaten the planet? Satish Kumar examines the often-overlooked relationship between everyday energy consumption and climate change, highlighting the enormous scale of electricity required to power our homes, vehicles and increasingly digital lives. From air conditioners and their temperature settings to the rapidly expanding energy demands of AI, social media and data centres, he reveals the hidden environmental cost of convenience and technological progress. Looking ahead to a projected surge in electricity consumption by 2050, the talk questions whether renewable energy alone can solve the problem, reminding us that even solar and wind power require significant material resources. Drawing on his organization’s work in energy-efficient home and transport design, Satish advocates a fundamental shift in thinking: instead of si
title: Nurturing Nature | Dr. Satish Kaumar | TEDxAIS Gurgaon 46 Youth

description: Ms. Kanika Sood engages in Social Entrepreneurship. Her take on the sustainability is the ESQ – Environmental Sensitive Quotient. Ms. Sood believes that it is imperative how you feel inside towards your environment that is where the thoughts towards the actual nurturing the nature begin. The realization that the conserving environment is not an external factor comes from the four pillars mentioned in her ESQ – Awareness – Emotion – Responsibility – Engagement – She in her talk dwells on the youth developing environmental anxiety and therefore confused as to where to begin the sustainability journey. Her take on the solutions in the talk and reminder that the environment conservation is not a one time event. Kanika Sood is a dynamic social entrepreneur encompassing roles as a creative producer, marketer, educator, social designer, brand builder, business strategist, and sustainability educator. title: Nurturing Nature | Kanika Sood | TEDxAIS Gurgaon 46 Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if environmental damage could be prevented instead of repaired? Sameera Satija, a former government employee who left her job to pursue her calling of safeguarding the environment, believes that meaningful change begins with simple, actionable steps. Her journey began with witnessing the deplorable conditions of villagers living beside a mountain of waste and recognizing the urgent need to rethink how waste is managed at its very source. From promoting zero-waste homes and teaching individuals to recycle and reduce landfill waste, she has worked to turn environmental awareness into practical green skills. Her most distinctive initiative, the Crockery Bank, addresses a seemingly small but widespread problem—the use of disposable and toxic plates at events. By purchasing steel crockery and making it available free of charge for events, her initiative encourages people to borrow, use, wash and return rather than consume and discard. What began as an individual response to an environ
title: Nurturing Nature | Sameera Satija | TEDxAIS Gurgaon 46 Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: As a Creative Environmentalist, Rumit Walia works with international organizations to create environmental awareness through innovative activities and activism. Challenging the conventional understanding of environmentalism, he presents a deceptively simple idea: the solution may not always be to do more, but to consume less, extract less and ultimately leave less of a footprint on the planet. From questioning the consumer mindset and advocating an anti-polythene approach to encouraging realistic, everyday behavioural change, his talk moves environmentalism from an abstract concern to a practical way of life. Walia explores the three pillars essential for meaningful change—governance, industries and individuals—and emphasizes that environmental action can only be effective when all three engage collectively. Rooted in simple thoughts and doable solutions, the talk invites us to reconsider what we buy, what we use and what we take from the Earth, reminding us that sometimes, conserving
title: Nurturing Nature | Rumit Walia | TEDxAIS Gurgaon 46 Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: In a world driven by consumer culture and an ever-expanding commercial economy, environmental conservation can no longer remain an optional choice. The talk explores the urgent need to rethink our relationship with commodities, resources and consumption, drawing from the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDGs 3, 7, 11 and 13. It examines how excessive consumption, inadequate recycling practices and our continued dependence on non-renewable sources of energy are placing an unsustainable burden on the planet. Emphasizing the principle of the 5 Rs, the talk moves beyond individual environmental responsibility to question how every profession, industry and economic activity can actively contribute to conservation. At its heart lies a call for stronger civic sense and a fundamental shift in the way we consume, work and live. The talk presents environmental sustainability not as a separate agenda, but as an imperative that must be woven into every aspect of society and the economy
title: Nurturing Nature | Priyam Jain | TEDxAIS Gurgaon 46 Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What does it truly take to build a powerful personal brand that drives real influence and opportunity? In this insightful presentation, Sudharsan Anganapathy breaks down personal branding from the ground up—moving beyond vanity metrics to focus on a strategic matrix of visibility, consistent value, trust, and category leadership.  

Discover how to transition from simply being known to being trusted, desired, and referred. Learn why success relies on robust systems rather than just goals, how to choose the right primary and secondary digital assets for your content, and how to measure your personal brand growth effectively.  Sudharshanan Ganapathy is a personal branding strategist and the founder and CEO of The Social Company. He went from being a freelancer in the digital marketing space to running his own agency in the domain. Sudharsanan got deeply involved in personal branding during the pandemic and rebranded The Social Company into a personal branding agency. Along with his team
title: Re-introducing Personal Branding:The Matrix, Systems and Strategy | Sudharsanan Ganapathy | TEDxKVEG

author: TEDx Talks
description: How can the automotive industry reinvent itself to meet the environmental and economic challenges of tomorrow? In this visionary talk, EV leader, technocrat, and entrepreneur Ajesh Saklecha explores the blueprint for Future Industries, focusing on connected, lean, and sustainable systems. Discover how data-driven design, smart manufacturing, micro-factory clusters, and innovations like India’s indigenously designed "Alice" EV platform are radically reducing carbon footprints, lowering capital expenditure, and pioneering a cleaner path forward for global transport. AJesh Saklecha, a serial entrepreneur and co-founder of Ozone Motors and triDE mobility, started his first profitable business at the age of 15. He is an inquisitive explorer who seeks opportunities to solve individual needs and has built multiple businesses spanning custom watches, computers, IT, electronic devices, entertainment media, and automobiles. title: Future Industries: Connected, Lean, and Sustainable Mobility | Ajesh Saklecha | TEDxKVEG

author: TEDx Talks
description: İpek Kuru Gönen, dikkatimizi, nefesimizi ve duygularımızı fark etmeyi öğrenmenin hem kendimizle hem de öğrenmeyle kurduğumuz ilişkiyi nasıl dönüştürebileceğini anlatıyor. Anadolu Üniversitesi Eğitim Fakültesi İngiliz Dili ve Eğitimi Anabilim Dalında öğretim üyesi olarak görev yapmaktadır. Eğitimin her kademesine İngilizce öğretmeni yetiştirmektedir. Ulusal ve uluslararası alanda dil öğretimi üzerine pek çok yayını ve ödülü bulunmakta ve eğitim projelerinde araştırmacı ve yürütücü olarak görev almaktadır. Son yıllarda özellikle yenilikçi öğrenme ve öğretme yöntemleri üzerine araştırmalar yapmakta ve araştırmacılar yetiştirmektedir. Bilinçli Farkındalık (Mindfulness) ve toplumun her kesimine hitap edecek eğitim programları tasarlamakta, ulusal ve uluslararası seminerler ve çalıştaylar düzenlemektedir. Tasarladığı web araçları ve mobil yeniliklerle bilinçli farkındalık uygulamalarını eşitlikçi ve hayat boyu öğrenmeyi destekleyici bir şekilde yaymak için seminer, eğitim ve konuşmalar düze
title: Zihnin Eski, Dünya Yeni | İpek Kuru Gönen | TEDxBalikesir Aci Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
“The Strangers Who Changed My Life” explores the unexpected connections we can form with animals we may never have known before. Through personal encounters with animals, this speech reveals how these seemingly brief and accidental moments can leave a lasting impact on the way we see life, compassion, and the world around us.
Sometimes, the most meaningful lessons come from the most unexpected strangers. Through stories of encounters with animals, the speech invites us to look beyond the human world and recognise the emotions, vulnerability, and resilience of the creatures who share our planet.
It is a heartfelt reflection on how animals can become teachers, companions, and catalysts for change—even when they enter our lives for only a moment. Umanda Pemarathne is an 11-year-old student from Hillwood College with a deep love for animals, plants, and the natural world. She enjoys caring for wounded animals and nurturing plants, reflecting her strong sense of compassion for living thing
title: The Strangers Who Changed My Life” | Umanda Pemarathne | TEDxKandy

author: TEDx Talks
description:
“You Are Someone’s Ancestor” invites us to look beyond the present and imagine ourselves as part of a much larger story. Every choice we make today has the potential to influence the people, communities, and world that come after us.
The speech explores the idea that we are not only shaped by the generations before us—we are also shaping the lives of generations yet to come. From the values we pass on to the choices we make about our environment, relationships, and society, our actions can leave a lasting legacy.
By asking us to see ourselves as someone’s ancestor, this thought-provoking talk challenges us to consider: What kind of world will we leave behind, and what will future generations remember about us? Shalini Senara De Silva is a student with a strong curiosity about psychology, human behaviour, and the many perspectives that shape the way we understand the world. Beyond her studies, she enjoys exploring new ideas, taking part in extracurricular activities, and developing her
title: You are someone's ancestor | Shalini Senara De Silva | TEDxKandy

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In a world where organisations are rapidly investing in AI, automation, robotics, and advanced technology, why do some companies still struggle to achieve sustainable transformation?

This talk explores the often-overlooked force behind successful transformation: human alignment. Drawing from decades of leadership and manufacturing experience, the speaker shares powerful lessons on purpose, ownership, continuous improvement, and leadership. Through stories inspired by the Bhagavad Gita, manufacturing excellence, martial arts, and personal leadership experiences, the talk demonstrates that technology can accelerate performance—but aligned people give transformation its direction and sustainability. Dr Shrikrishan Yogi is a group CEO & director of a major auto parts manufacturing group; he is leading a bold transformation through Vision 2030, a journey to reimagine a traditional manufacturing company into a global, future-ready solution provider. But beyond numbers and growth, his missi
title: The Power of Alignment | Dr. Shrikrishan Yogi | TEDxMoulsari Avenue

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Ignoring the 10%: Finding My Voice is a personal and inspiring journey about growing up with speech delay and learning to communicate with confidence.
Thinuk shares how being told that he was behind the expected milestones could have become the definition of who he was. Instead, he learned to focus not on the 10% he could not do yet, but on the 90% of possibilities ahead of him.
The talk explores the emotional challenges of speech delay—from frustration and self-doubt to feeling different from others—and the determination it took to overcome them. More importantly, it is about discovering that finding your voice is not simply about speaking clearly; it is about having the courage to express who you are and what you believe.
Through his story, Thinuk hopes to encourage children and young people facing communication challenges to stop measuring themselves against others, recognize their own progress, and keep moving forward.
Because sometimes, finding your voice begins with refusing to
title: Ignoring the 10% to find my voice  | Thinuk Gunaratne | TEDxKandy

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The Fold That Shaped Me explores how something as simple as a sheet of paper can become a powerful teacher.
In this personal and inspiring talk, Dillon Alexander shares how discovering origami changed the way he thinks, learns, and sees the world. What began as folding paper gradually became a lesson in patience, precision, creativity, resilience, and problem-solving. Every fold has a purpose, and every mistake is an opportunity to unfold, learn, and try again.
Through his journey with origami, Dillon discovered that creating something meaningful does not always require expensive tools or complicated technology. Sometimes, all it takes is a simple piece of paper—and the willingness to make the first fold.

title: The fold that shaped me | Dillon Alexander | TEDxKandy
